english.notes:
Subsection 2(3) and (4) of the Act provide:-
2(3) A person does not commit an offence under subsection (1) if-
(a) the interview referred to in that subsection takes place after the person has entered the United Kingdom, and (b) within the period of three days beginning with the date of the interview the person provides to an immigration officer or to the Secretary of State a document of the kind referred to in that subsection.
2(4) of the Act provides that it is a defence for a person charged with this offence
(a) to prove that he is an EEA national,
(b) to prove that he is a member of the family of an EEA national and that he is exercising a right under retained EU law in respect of entry to or residence in the United Kingdom,
(c) to prove that he has a reasonable excuse for not being in possession of a document of the kind specified in subsection (1),
(d) to produce a false immigration document and to prove that he used that document as an immigration document for all purposes in connection with his journey to the United Kingdom, or
(e) to prove that he travelled to the United Kingdom without, at any stage since he set out on the journey, having possession of an immigration document,
(f) the fact that a document was deliberately destroyed or disposed of is not a reasonable excuse unless it can be shown that this was for a reasonable cause or beyond the control of the person,
(g) reasonable cause does not include for the purposes of delaying the handling or resolution of a claim, increasing the chances of success of a claim or application or complying with the instructions or advice given by an agent or facilitator (unless in the circumstances it would be unreasonable to expect non-compliance).

other.penalty:
Either way

Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and /or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 2(9)(b) and (15) of the Asylum and Immigration (Treatment of Claimants, etc.) Act 2004 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit on prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
